Reflection summary:

The failure was a 0.001 last-digit error on the intercept only (−184.142 vs −184.143); the slope (0.096) was perfect. This is genuinely generalizable, not per-question trivia:

Root cause: With an untransformed calendar-year predictor (mean_x ≈ 1935), the intercept = mean_y − slope·mean_x amplifies any slope-precision error by ~2000×. A 5e-7 slope error becomes a 0.001 intercept error — exactly one thousandths-place unit. So computing the intercept from a rounded slope, or any intermediate rounding, corrupts the intercept's last digit even when the slope still rounds correctly.

Fix recorded: Fit once at full float64 precision (np.polyfit / linregress), then round slope and intercept independently from the full-precision fit — never derive the intercept from the rounded slope, and keep the literal years given (re-basing is slope-invariant but intercept-changing).
